newsitem.title: ITALY: Leading Mafia turncoat arrested on drugs charges.
newsitem.headline: Leading Mafia turncoat arrested on drugs charges.

text.p: Salvatore Contorno, one of the most important Mafia turncoats, has been arrested on suspicion of trafficking in drugs while part of a witness protection programme, Italy's top anti-Mafia official said on Wednesday.
Contorno's arrest was announced at a news conference in Rome by PierLuigi Vigna, Italy's national anti-Mafia prosecutor.
Vigna said Contorno had been arrested on suspicion that he had trafficked in drugs between 1990 and 1993, when he was already part of a witness protection programme.

Contorno, the most important "pentito," or turncoat, after Tommaso Buscetta, began cooperating with investigators in 1984. His testimony led to the arrests of hundreds of Mafiosi and the dismantling of many drug refineries in Sicily.
Contorno also cooperated with American investigators prosecuting the U.S. Mafia.
The Sicilian Mafia killed a number of his relatives in retaliation for his collaboration with police and tried to kill Contorno in 1993 when he was living in a safe house hear Rome.
His arrest was bound to reopen a debate about the controversial role of turncoats in the state's fight against the Mafia.
